title: In 2021 it was raining fish in Texas: How a storm sparked a social media frenzy and a strange wildlife mystery wrapped in theories
excerpt: In a remarkable event on December 29, 2021, Texarkana residents witnessed an astonishing phenomenon as fish fell from the sky. An abundance of dead gizzard shad littered the area, prompting various explanations to surface. Among these was the idea of avian involvement. Despite rumors of a waterspout, no such occurrence was logged, keeping the actual cause of the fish's arrival shrouded in intrigue.
content:
What happened in Texas’ Texarkana on December 29, 2021, left people in absolute shock. A day when everyone saw raining fishes as thunderstorms pounded the skies over Texarkana. According to BBC Wildlife Magazine’s Discover Wildlife, a plethora of little silvery fish fell across an area of approximately nine square miles. Hundreds of fishes that landed on the ground were seen spread across roads, lawns, parking lots, garage forecourts, and roofs. All of them were dead.

The phenomenon that transpired that day was bizarre in many ways, but apparently it was not the first time that something of this magnitude has occurred. According to BBC Wildlife, there have been accounts of ‘animal rain,' which date back centuries. Besides fish, there are claims that frogs, toads, worms, and even spiders fell from above.



Several theories emerged

The event of raining fishes made it to the headlines and flooded social media platforms with photos and videos, paving the way for multiple theories. The buzz created by the surprising incident apparently made it perhaps the most documented fish fall in history. BBC Wildlife reported that the fish were all gizzard shad. They are freshwater species common in Texas.

How did fishes get into the sky?

Initially many thought that it was due to a waterspout. This is a common belief in cases of animal rains. National Ocean Service defines a waterspout as a whirling column of air and water mist.

A whirling column of air and mist can lift small aquatic animals out of the water and carry them into the sky. As a result, what went up came down. However, this theory fell flat, as no waterspout was recorded near Texarkana.

Several possibilities were taken into consideration. It was perhaps the storm that may have blown fish out of a nearby pond. Or they might have fallen from an aircraft. None of this actually made sense. But a fresh clue emerged that changed everything.

According to BBC Wildlife Magazine, some of the shad showed signs of being partially digested. The runway cleaning staff of the airport, which cleared fishes from the runways, noticed something. Fishes were “kind of chewed up.” Scores of cormorants and fish-eating birds were spotted nearby. These birds swallow their prey whole and are known to regurgitate their food when disturbed.

The theory here was that the fish hadn't been caught up by the storm. They’d been coughed up by cormorants. This seemed plausible for a short span of time, but like other theories, this also remained unproven. There were no sightings of cormorants regurgitating the fish.
